families.name: Adaptive piecewise response models
families.question: Does a small mixture of local response functions capture heterogeneity missed by one global model?
families.experiment: Compare a soft-gated mixture with one linear model and a capacity-matched nonlinear baseline on the same rows and split.
families.pitfalls: Tiny effective segments can overfit; check per-segment support and latency.

families.name: Prediction-to-decision mapping
families.question: Would a different action rule improve the declared business objective with the same predictions?
families.experiment: Freeze the predictor and validation protocol; compare a threshold, score fusion or feasible-set rule against the current decision rule.
families.pitfalls: A higher click score is not an incremental treatment effect; use observed value and cost only when their definitions are valid.

families.name: Typed knowledge-graph retrieval
families.question: Do typed entity relations add retrieval signal beyond interaction and item-side baselines?
families.experiment: Hold the candidate pool and evaluation protocol fixed; ablate relation-aware information against matched item representations.
families.pitfalls: Entity links or graph edges formed after the evaluation cutoff leak future information.

families.name: Graph neighborhood and proximity representations
families.question: Do supplied graph neighborhoods or proximity objectives add signal beyond independent item features?
families.experiment: Keep the data cutoff, labels, candidate universe and evaluator fixed; replace one model component with a simple control and compare held-out slices.
families.pitfalls: Graph/position/popularity inputs require explicit provenance; structural assumptions alone do not identify causal effects.

families.name: Logged-feedback factorization
families.question: Does explicit exposure or popularity factorization improve the declared prediction target under supported assumptions?
families.experiment: Keep the data cutoff, labels, candidate universe and evaluator fixed; replace one model component with a simple control and compare held-out slices.
families.pitfalls: Graph/position/popularity inputs require explicit provenance; structural assumptions alone do not identify causal effects.

families.name: Query-group ranking objectives
families.question: Does a grouped ranking objective improve ordering with the same scores, labels and candidate universe?
families.experiment: Hold backbone and queries fixed; compare pointwise loss, RankNet and detached DeltaNDCG-weighted pairs.
families.pitfalls: Cross-query pairs, padded candidates and metric weights with unsupported relevance labels invalidate the comparison.

families.name: Representation diagnostics and feature screening
families.question: Which observed representation or input-use bottleneck warrants a local experiment?
families.experiment: Inspect supplied training activations and gradients, state competing explanations, then change one component or protected feature group with a matched ablation and retraining.
families.pitfalls: Effective rank, saliency and cosine similarity are diagnostics, not causal importance or proof of task improvement. Do not prune interaction-only fields from marginal scores.

families.name: Discount-aware marketing and conversion response
families.question: Does pre-decision discount history or purchase preference explain residual response variation within the current backbone?
families.experiment: Use the existing interest representation; isolate a discount branch, its history/user/context components, and a separately weighted purchase-only regression objective under a fixed evaluation protocol.
families.pitfalls: Realized current-order discounts are labels, not serving inputs. Missing or future histories, mixed ratio definitions and conversion-to-uplift claims invalidate conclusions.

families.name: Supervised auxiliary objectives and parameter penalties
families.question: Does an isolated objective or regularization change improve learning with the current backbone and inputs?
families.experiment: Hold data version, split, target, backbone and budget fixed; change one local component and measure the declared falsification criterion.
families.pitfalls: Input readiness is a declaration, not evidence of correct integration, causal identification or improved held-out utility.

families.name: Aligned pretrained and learned input representations
families.question: Do aligned pretrained representations improve supported cold or sparse slices under a fixed vocabulary contract?
families.experiment: Hold data version, split, target, backbone and budget fixed; change one local component and measure the declared falsification criterion.
families.pitfalls: Input readiness is a declaration, not evidence of correct integration, causal identification or improved held-out utility.

families.name: Paired prediction quality diagnostics
families.question: Does a paired prediction comparison support a ranking, confidence or class-loss hypothesis before changing the model?
families.experiment: Observe baseline and candidate on identical ordered unique sample IDs, dataset/split identity and weights. Use the unchanged task metric and independent holdout policy; fit any calibration only on a separate permitted split.
families.pitfalls: Sample IDs, labels or weights are not paired; scores are logits instead of probabilities; a single-class AUC is invented; clipping artifacts or class-mix changes are presented as a proven explanation or significant uplift.
